newsitem.title: USA: Study says NYC subway signs confusing.
newsitem.headline: Study says NYC subway signs confusing.

text.p: A new study shows that more than a third of New York City's subway stations have signs that are confusing, wrong or simply missing.

In news that should come as little surprise to any visitor to New York City, the study released Tuesday by the New York City Transit Riders Council found problems at 82 of 100 randomly selected stations. The volunteer group appointed by the governor represents the interests of subways and riders.
The group released its findings at the 86th Street station, which features signs for the "CC" and "K" subway lines. Both lines were discontinued more than a decade ago.
At station entrances and token-vending booths, the most common problem was a lack of signs indicating the subway lines below by letter or number, it said.

One-fifth of the subway entrances were missing the coloured globes that indicate whether a station is open full- or part-time, the group said. But that's an improvement from 10 years ago when globes at half the stations were missing the globes, it said.
The group said overall, subway signs have improved since its 1987 study but added that many new signs contain errors and some signs were updated with decals that have since peeled off.
